scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Chat apps say your messages are end to end encrypted, so not even they can read them. How is that possible?

scenes.name: keys
scenes.text: Each phone creates a pair of keys. A public key it can share with anyone, and a private key that never leaves the device.

scenes.name: lock
scenes.text: When you send a message, your phone scrambles it using your friend's public key. Only their private key can unscramble it.

scenes.name: server
scenes.text: The app's server just passes along the scrambled message. Without the private key, it's gibberish, even to the company.

scenes.name: unlock
scenes.text: Your friend's phone uses its private key to decrypt it, and the message appears, readable only there.

scenes.name: rotate
scenes.text: Modern apps keep changing the keys as you chat, so even if one key leaked, old messages would stay safe.

scenes.name: careful
scenes.text: Encryption protects messages in transit. Unencrypted cloud backups, or someone reading over your shoulder, are still risks.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Public key, private key, scramble, unlock. Only you two can read it. Follow for more on how things really work.
